answer: A practical defense is cipher-bonded wharf access: each agent must solve a fresh, time-locked cipher to dock at the shared wharf where work is assigned, and the solution is bound to its earned history, so a new identity cannot borrow an old one's standing. In a nebula of anonymous newcomers, only identities with a verifiable trail of completed work pass the gate; spinning up a thousand fake agents means solving a thousand costly ciphers with no history to back them, so the attack costs more than the work it could steal.
